findings.name: KeePass
findings.summary: KeePass Password Safe is a free and open-source password manager primarily for Windows. It officially supports macOS and Linux operating systems through the use of Mono. Additionally, there are several unofficial ports for Windows Phone, Android, iOS, and BlackBerry devices, which normally work with the same copied or shared (remote) password database. KeePass stores usernames, passwords, and other fields, including free-form notes and file attachments, in an encrypted file. This file can be protected by any combination of a master password, a key file, and the current Windows account details. By default, the KeePass database is stored on a local file system.
findings.pricing: Free and open-source (GPL v2), zero subscription fee or software cost.
findings.pricing_evidence: KeePass Password Safe is free and open-source software under the GPL v2 license with zero subscription fees.
findings.supported_platforms: Official: Windows (native 7/8/10/11); macOS & Linux (via Mono/Wine). Contributed/Unofficial Ports: Android (KeePassDroid, KeePass2Android, KeePassDX), iOS (Strongbox, KyPass).
findings.supported platforms: Official: Windows (native 7/8/10/11); macOS & Linux (via Mono/Wine). Contributed/Unofficial Ports: Android (KeePassDroid, KeePass2Android, KeePassDX), iOS (Strongbox, KyPass).
findings.platform_evidence: Official download documentation states native Windows 7-11 support, Mono/Wine for macOS/Linux, and contributed ports for Android/iOS.
findings.strengths: Free and open-source with local offline database storage, portable installation, zero cloud dependence, and extensible plugin architecture.
findings.strength_evidence: Features list highlights offline encrypted database file, zero cloud server dependencies, portable installation, and open plugin architecture under GPL v2.
findings.weaknesses: Cloud synchronization depends on external storage integration or plugins when the storage provider is not accessible through KeePass-supported protocols.
findings.weakness_evidence: KeePass synchronization documentation confirms native file and URL synchronization across supported protocols, while unsupported storage providers or cloud systems rely on external integrations or third-party plugins.
